subject: Transient service blips on 2028-05-31 — credit eligibility & RCA timeline
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex@lumino-payments.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient service blips on 2028-05-31 — impact and ask

Hi Kimberly,

We observed a short cluster of 503/timeout responses affecting our production traffic that hit our customer-facing payment routes on 2028-05-31. The spike was brief but noticeable: roughly 18:22:00Z to 18:29:00Z (UTC) across us-west1 (we see a few hundred failed requests and elevated tail latencies).

Can you confirm whether this was a platform-side availability blip (as opposed to a client-side retry storm) and whether it would be eligible for SLA credit under our agreement? We've attached a small sample of traces and an aggregated error snapshot.

Attachments included: error-snapshot-20280531.log, request-trace-503.json.gz, sla-lookup-202805.csv

What we need from Redwood:
- Confirmed impacted window (start/end) from your side
- Cause classification (service unavailable vs. throttling vs. client-side)
- Whether this meets the SLA threshold for a credit and an estimate for credit amount
- ETA for a postmortem / RCA we can share with our ops team (we're aiming for an internal incident review tomorrow morning)

Thanks — this is high-priority for our on-call. If helpful, looping in our SRE distribution: sre@lumino-payments.com.

—Alex Carter
Head of Platform, Lumino Payments
alex@lumino-payments.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex@lumino-payments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient service blips on 2028-05-31 — impact and ask

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments.

We’ve ingested the logs you sent and I’ve routed this to our infra on-call. Initial ask for us to triage: could you confirm whether you saw elevated retry traffic around the window you listed? That helps us rule out client-side amplification. Either way, we will do an internal impact window verification and pull the KV/cache traces for that timeframe.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Rishi (CC) will validate the exact impacted window from our telemetry and return an initial impact summary.
- We’ll check whether the symptom aligns with an SLA-eligible service outage (per our Availability SLO definitions) and estimate any credit.
- We aim to provide an initial incident summary and an internal RCA draft within 72 hours; a formal postmortem will follow.

I’ll keep you posted. If this is blocking your incident review timeline, tell me and I’ll prioritize the postmortem draft.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex@lumino-payments.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient service blips on 2028-05-31 — impact and ask

Alex / Kimberly — quick technical follow-up from the infra side. Quoting Kimberly below for context.

On Thu, Jun 1, 2028 at 10:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments.

Summary of internal findings (preliminary):
- We validated a short availability degradation window between 2028-05-31T18:22:05Z and 2028-05-31T18:29:12Z (UTC) across nodes serving us-west1.
- Root symptom: a transient KV-cache eviction cascade after a rolling kernel patch triggered higher mem reclaim pressure on a subset of serving hosts. That led to elevated tail latencies and ~1.2% of requests returning 503 for that ~7-minute window.
- No evidence of customer-side retry storms; request rates were within expected bounds for Lumino.

Evidence attached: request-trace-503.json.gz (sample traces), error-snapshot-20280531.log, plus service-side heap/mem traces (attached to INF-1234).

SLA/credit guidance: based on the verified >=1-minute service availability gap and the Agreement terms (Availability SLO and credit calculation), this event appears eligible for standard pro-rated credit. We will calculate the credit using the SLO window and your usage for that billing period and provide a documented calculation.

Next steps & ETA: 
- I’ll file a formal incident ticket (INF-1234) and add the full evidence pack.
- Draft RCA and credit calc: target within 72 hours (by 2028-06-04 EOD PT).
- Final postmortem and compensatory credit issuance: target within 10 business days, unless further investigation extends this.

If Lumino needs an interim statement for your internal review tomorrow, I can provide a one-paragraph summary you can share.

—Rishi
Senior Principal — Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Carter <alex@lumino-payments.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient service blips on 2028-05-31 — impact and ask

Thanks Kim and Rishi — that’s helpful and appreciated.

Please proceed with the calculation and INF-1234 evidence pack. For our incident review, a short interim note that confirms the window and that you’re treating this as an SLA-impacting event will suffice. If you can share the credit calculation format (line items) that we should expect, that will speed procurement’s review.

We’ll share any additional metrics we pull overnight but it sounds like you have the core artifacts. Looking forward to the RCA draft by 2028-06-04.

—Alex
Head of Platform, Lumino Payments
